en.name: Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (PEEP)
en.shortDescription: Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) applied by the ventilator: set, displayed or extrinsic PEEP, in cmH2O. Intrinsic and total PEEP have their own sets.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) is the pressure the ventilator maintains in the airways at the end of expiration, to keep alveoli open and improve oxygenation [1, 2]. Most ventilated patients with ARDS receive 5 to 12 cmH2O [2]. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, set on the ventilator or displayed by it, in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar). This set holds the **applied** PEEP, also called extrinsic PEEP. The ventilator measures the pressure in its circuit, not in the alveoli, so a PEEP recorded without qualification is the applied PEEP [1]. The alveolar pressure measured during an end-expiratory hold (total PEEP) and its excess over the applied PEEP (intrinsic PEEP, or auto-PEEP) are distinct variables with their own sets: *Total Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (Total PEEP)* and *Intrinsic Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (auto-PEEP)*. ## Included Concepts The set lists the five standard LOINC concepts of the applied PEEP, all in the Measurement domain. - *3016226 / 20075-8 — PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)*: the generic concept; the default. - *21490855 / 76248-4 — PEEP Respiratory system --on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same value, explicitly recorded on a ventilator. - *3022875 / 20077-4 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator (LOINC)*: the PEEP set on the ventilator. - *42528515 / 83386-3 — Extrinsic PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)*: the applied PEEP, labelled as extrinsic, typically next to an intrinsic or total PEEP measurement. - *42528516 / 83387-1 — Extrinsic dynamic PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)*: LOINC publishes no definition; the code is an import of the IEEE 11073 device term `MDC_PRESS_AWAY_END_EXP_POS_EXTRINSIC_DYNAMIC` [3]. **Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar). ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records a PEEP without qualification: *3016226 / 20075-8 — PEEP Respiratory system*. The PEEP set on the ventilator maps to *3022875 / 20077-4 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator*. - **Extrinsic PEEP**: *42528515 / 83386-3 — Extrinsic PEEP Respiratory system* when the source labels the value as extrinsic; *42528516 / 83387-1 — Extrinsic dynamic PEEP Respiratory system* only when it is explicitly labelled dynamic. - **Not intrinsic or total PEEP**: auto-PEEP belongs to the *Intrinsic Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (auto-PEEP)* set, and the pressure read during an end-expiratory hold to the *Total Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (Total PEEP)* set. - **Not other airway pressures**: peak, plateau and mean airway pressures have their own concept sets. - **Setting and displayed value share one set**: they are one protocol variable, and sources often record one or the other without a reliable label. Go down to the concept_id for an analysis that needs the distinction. ## References [1] Brochard L. Intrinsic (or auto-) PEEP during controlled mechanical ventilation. Intensive Care Med. 2002;28(10):1376-8. Available: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00134-002-1438-8 [2] Brower RG, Lanken PN, MacIntyre N, et al. Higher versus lower positive end-expiratory pressures in patients with the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2004;351(4):327-36. Available: https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa032193 [3] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC/IEEE Medical Device Code Mapping Table, distributed with the LOINC release (`AccessoryFiles/LoincIeeeMedicalDeviceCodeMappingTable`). Maps LOINC 83387-1 to IEEE 11073-10101 `MDC_PRESS_AWAY_END_EXP_POS_EXTRINSIC_DYNAMIC` (152792) as `equivalent`. Available: https://loinc.org/downloads/

fr.name: Pression expiratoire positive (PEP)
fr.shortDescription: Pression expiratoire positive (PEP) appliquée par le ventilateur : PEP réglée, affichée ou extrinsèque, en cmH2O. Les PEP intrinsèque et totale ont leurs propres sets.
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique La pression expiratoire positive (PEP, ou PEEP) est la pression que le ventilateur maintient dans les voies aériennes en fin d’expiration, pour maintenir les alvéoles ouvertes et améliorer l’oxygénation [1, 2]. La plupart des patients ventilés pour un SDRA reçoivent 5 à 12 cmH2O [2]. Dans les données sources, c’est une valeur numérique unique par patient et par horodatage, réglée sur le ventilateur ou affichée par lui, en centimètres d’eau (cmH2O) ; certains ventilateurs affichent des mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0,98 mbar). Ce set contient la PEP **appliquée**, dite aussi PEP extrinsèque. Le ventilateur mesure la pression dans son circuit, pas dans les alvéoles : une PEP enregistrée sans précision est donc la PEP appliquée [1]. La pression alvéolaire mesurée pendant une pause télé-expiratoire (PEP totale) et son excès sur la PEP appliquée (PEP intrinsèque, ou auto-PEP) sont des variables distinctes, avec leurs propres sets : *Pression expiratoire positive totale (PEP totale)* et *Pression expiratoire positive intrinsèque (auto-PEP)*. ## Concepts inclus Le set liste les cinq concepts LOINC standard de la PEP appliquée, tous du domaine Measurement. - *3016226 / 20075-8 — PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)* : le concept générique, à utiliser par défaut. - *21490855 / 76248-4 — PEEP Respiratory system --on ventilator (LOINC)* : la même valeur, explicitement recueillie sous ventilateur. - *3022875 / 20077-4 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator (LOINC)* : la PEP réglée sur le ventilateur. - *42528515 / 83386-3 — Extrinsic PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)* : la PEP appliquée, qualifiée d’extrinsèque, en général à côté d’une mesure de PEP intrinsèque ou totale. - *42528516 / 83387-1 — Extrinsic dynamic PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)* : LOINC n’en publie pas de définition ; le code est repris du terme IEEE 11073 `MDC_PRESS_AWAY_END_EXP_POS_EXTRINSIC_DYNAMIC` [3]. **Unités** : en **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), l’unité recommandée, avec une conversion cmH2O↔mbar enregistrée (1 cmH2O = 0,98 mbar). ## Notes de mapping - **Concept par défaut** quand la source enregistre une PEP sans précision : *3016226 / 20075-8 — PEEP Respiratory system*. La PEP réglée sur le ventilateur se mappe sur *3022875 / 20077-4 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator*. - **PEP extrinsèque** : *42528515 / 83386-3 — Extrinsic PEEP Respiratory system* quand la source qualifie la valeur d’extrinsèque ; *42528516 / 83387-1 — Extrinsic dynamic PEEP Respiratory system* seulement si elle est explicitement qualifiée de dynamique. - **Pas la PEP intrinsèque ni la PEP totale** : l’auto-PEP relève du set *Pression expiratoire positive intrinsèque (auto-PEP)*, et la pression lue pendant une pause télé-expiratoire du set *Pression expiratoire positive totale (PEP totale)*. - **Pas les autres pressions des voies aériennes** : les pressions de crête, de plateau et moyenne ont leurs propres concept sets. - **Réglage et valeur affichée partagent un même set** : c’est une seule variable de protocole, et les sources enregistrent souvent l’un ou l’autre sans étiquette fiable. Descendre au concept_id pour une analyse qui a besoin de la distinction. ## Références [1] Brochard L. Intrinsic (or auto-) PEEP during controlled mechanical ventilation. Intensive Care Med. 2002;28(10):1376-8. Available: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00134-002-1438-8 [2] Brower RG, Lanken PN, MacIntyre N, et al. Higher versus lower positive end-expiratory pressures in patients with the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2004;351(4):327-36. Available: https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa032193 [3] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC/IEEE Medical Device Code Mapping Table, distributed with the LOINC release (`AccessoryFiles/LoincIeeeMedicalDeviceCodeMappingTable`). Maps LOINC 83387-1 to IEEE 11073-10101 `MDC_PRESS_AWAY_END_EXP_POS_EXTRINSIC_DYNAMIC` (152792) as `equivalent`. Available: https://loinc.org/downloads/

reviews.comments: As for minute volume (concept set 317), this set mixes the PEEP ventilator setting with the measured PEEP. During invasive ventilation, are the set PEEP and the measured PEEP the same thing?

reviewer.affiliation: Univ Rennes, CHU Rennes, INSERM, LTSI-UMR 1099, Rennes, France
reviewer.profession: Medical Informatics and Intensive Care Physician

reviews.comments: Reply to Maxim Moinat's review. Set and measured PEEP are indeed not the same thing: under auto-PEEP the measured total PEEP exceeds the set PEEP, and that gap is itself the clinical signal. They stay in one set all the same, since they are one protocol variable and the same datum surfaces as a setting or as a measurement depending on the centre, the ventilator and the mode, often without a reliable label. An analysis that turns on the distinction should go down to the concept_id. The Mapping Notes now explain this.

## Summary
**No verdict (comment).** Why use LOINC and SNOMED CT codes that mean the same?

## Use in our quality indicators
- Used in QI01 (Lung-protective ventilation in ARDS).
- CQL: 3 of 7 concepts are referenced in [`IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1): [4216746](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L58), [4353713](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L59), [42527140](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L57) (each ID links to its code definition).
- Not used by our indicators and not reviewed individually (4): 3022875 Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator, 3035822 Intrinsic PEEP Respiratory system, 4160171 Best positive end expiratory pressure, 42528515 Extrinsic PEEP Respiratory system.


## Suggestions
- Use just either the LOINC or the SNOMED CT codes, not both
Total PEEP should be distinguished where possible.

reviewer.affiliation: Univ Rennes, CHU Rennes, INSERM, LTSI-UMR 1099, Rennes, France
reviewer.profession: Medical Informatics and Intensive Care Physician

reviews.comments:
**Reply to the reviews of Gregor Lichtner and Nicolas Terzi**

- **LOINC and SNOMED codes meaning the same** (Gregor): we normally keep both when both are standard, so that every site is captured whichever vocabulary it mapped to. Here, v1.2.0 drops the two SNOMED concepts, **4353713** *Positive end expiratory pressure* and **4216746** *Positive end expiratory pressure setting*, because they sit in the Observation domain while the rest of the set is in Measurement. Note for QI01: your CQL still references these two concepts; their counterparts in the set are **3016226** *PEEP Respiratory system* and **3022875** *Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator*.
- **Total PEEP** (Nicolas): done in v1.4.0. Intrinsic and total PEEP now have their own concept sets, *Intrinsic Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (auto-PEEP)* (384) and *Total Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (Total PEEP)* (385), each with its static and dynamic concepts. This set keeps the applied PEEP: generic, on ventilator, ventilator setting and extrinsic PEEP. A PEEP recorded without qualification stays here: it is the set PEEP, or the end-expiratory pressure displayed by the ventilator, which matches it since auto-PEEP only shows during an end-expiratory occlusion.

Gregor: QI01 references **42527140** *Total PEEP Respiratory system*, which now belongs to set 385. For lung-protective ventilation, does QI01 need the total PEEP or the applied PEEP?

Could you check v1.4.3 and update your verdicts?

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Describe PEEP; add Best PEEP (4160171). Register cmH2O recommended unit + cmH2O<->mbar conversion. 7 concepts (generic, setting, best, extrinsic/intrinsic/total). LOINC sources.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Drop the conversion instruction from the mapping notes: the conversion is registered in unit_conversions.json and applied by the SQL export, so restating it as a manual step is redundant.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Mapping Notes: explain why the set PEEP and the measured PEEP live in one set rather than two, including the auto-PEEP caveat. Raised by Maxim Moinat, who asked whether they are the same thing. No change to the expression.

versions.author: Gregor Lichtner
versions.message: Keep the LOINC Measurement concepts only; drop the SNOMED concepts of the Observation domain.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Add the generic LOINC PEEP concepts (3016226 PEEP Respiratory system, default; 21490855 PEEP Respiratory system --on ventilator) and the dynamic extrinsic/intrinsic/total PEEP (42528516, 42527139, 42528517). Set now holds the 9 standard LOINC Measurement PEEP concepts, excluding ventilator limit and alarm settings.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Split intrinsic and total PEEP into their own concept sets, Intrinsic PEEP (auto-PEEP) (384) and Total PEEP (385), following Nicolas Terzi's review: they are distinct quantities, measured by a deliberate manoeuvre. Removed 3035822, 42527139 (intrinsic) and 42527140, 42528517 (total). The set now holds the applied PEEP: generic, on ventilator, ventilator setting, extrinsic (static and dynamic). Description rewritten with literature references.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Description: the two new sets are now named Intrinsic Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (auto-PEEP) and Total Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (Total PEEP); the ventilator display and the expiratory hold are now sourced to Brochard 2002 (Intensive Care Med), read in full. Concepts unchanged.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Description: the ESICM 2023 guidelines, now read in full, are cited for the Berlin PEEP threshold and for making no recommendation on PEEP titration strategy; the extrinsic dynamic PEEP is described only by its IEEE 11073 term, LOINC giving no definition. Concepts unchanged.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Description shortened to the level of detail of the other ventilation sets (definition, what to map where, analysis cautions); detailed physiology and measurement technique dropped. Concepts unchanged.
